proof.criterion: The tester's first failure — the section claimed the sequence's published last line is refused in this deployment. It is not: `kubectl get jobs,pods` runs and exits 0; it is asking for Services as well that is refused.
proof.surface: The live cluster from this role container, the published line run exactly as written and then with Services added.
proof.command: kubectl get jobs,pods ; kubectl get jobs,pods,svc ; kubectl auth can-i list jobs | list pods | list services | get services
proof.observed: `kubectl get jobs,pods` exits **0** and prints its table (twenty lines, not quoted: they are the namespace's other work). `kubectl get jobs,pods,svc` exits **1** with `Error from server (Forbidden): services is forbidden: … cannot list resource "services"` — the Services part alone. `list jobs` and `list pods` answer `yes`; `list services` and `get services` answer `no`. The clause now says the line runs as published and that adding Services is what is refused, because this identity may no more list a Service than create one.
proof.negativeControl: The refusal is the control for the claim: the same command with one more resource name changes the status from 0 to 1, which is the distinction the old clause collapsed. The grant matrix behind it is measured rather than inferred — `list` and `get` are asked separately, since this identity already proved they do not follow one another (`delete jobs` yes while `patch jobs` no).

proof.criterion: The tester's second failure — the evidence-boundary passage listed creating the Job, the wait, the logs and the delete among the steps executed nowhere, while the tester had run all four here and the record saying so is in the same commit.
proof.surface: The live cluster from this role container: the section's own Job manifest, run for real at this head, not a dry run.
proof.command: kubectl apply -f <the section's Job, its placeholders filled> ; kubectl get job … -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}' ; kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l job-name=… ; kubectl logs -l job-name=… --tail=2 ; kubectl delete job … ; kubectl get jobs,pods
proof.observed: `job.batch/infra-71-impl-check created`; the uid is 36 characters; the pod reaches Ready in **79 s** (the tester measured 1 m 24 s on its own run); the log tail is the server's own `database system is ready to accept connections`; `job.batch "infra-71-impl-check" deleted`; and the last line shows nothing of it left. The passage now lists the Job half as executed — applied and created, uid read, Ready in about eighty seconds, log line read, deleted, nothing left — and names only the Service steps as unexecuted, refused rather than untried, with the reachability check against a real workload as the one step that depends on them.
proof.negativeControl: The Service step is the control that keeps the new claim honest: at the same head, `kubectl apply` of the section's Service still ends `Forbidden` on the read of the live object before any create is attempted, so the passage's remaining 'not executed' entry is measured in the same session as its 'executed' ones. Housekeeping measured too: the Job carried a fifteen-minute deadline and a five-minute ttl, was deleted by hand, and `kubectl get jobs,pods` shows nothing of mine; the namespace's other work was not touched and is quoted nowhere.
